newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli-Palestinian unrest in Hebron, Jerusalem.
newsitem.headline: Israeli-Palestinian unrest in Hebron, Jerusalem.

text.p: Israeli soldiers on Friday fired rubber bullets to disperse Palestinian stone-throwers on a ninth day of protests against Jewish settlement construction in Arab East Jerusalem, witnesses said.

Hospitals said 25 Palestinians were treated for rubber bullet wounds and two for live bullet wounds during the clash in the West Bank town of Hebron which is split between Israeli and PLO rule. Palestinian police helped to contain the riot.

On Jerusalem's Temple Mount, Palestinians pelted Israeli police with stones after Friday Moslem prayers at al-Aqsa mosque. Police held their fire while guards from the Islamic Trust helped to disperse the stone-throwers.

During the incident police briefly evacuated Jewish worshippers from the sacred Wailing Wall below the mount for fear they might be stoned. Some policemen were lightly injured in the stone-throwing but none required hospital care.

U.S. presidential envoy Dennis Ross shuttled between Israelis and Palestinians hoping to rescue Middle East peacemaking, which plunged into crisis over Israel's groundbreaking for the settlement of 6,500 homes for Jews.

Palestinians want a stop to the hilltop settlement which Israelis call Har Homa and the Arabs call Jabal Abu Ghneim. Israel demands an end to violence that climaxed a week ago when a suicide bomber killed three women at a Tel Aviv cafe.
